text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

With London closed the market in New York was fairly dull. July and October lost 1 point to close at 10.79 cents/lb and 10.66 cents/lb respectively. The outer months lost between 1 and 5 points. There was no fresh news to influence prices. Traders said producer selling is likely to cap any price rise. Moreover, there is still a substantial speculative net long position in July. Open interest in July stood at 75,644 lots, down 6,768 lots as of early Friday.

MAURITIUS - Sugar exports in February 1997 amounted to 45,399 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 22,237 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first three quarters of 1996/97 (June/February) up to 569,920 tonnes against 514,933 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 565,608 tonnes compared to 525,697 tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in June/February 1996/97 were the United Kingdom with 438,553 tonnes raws against 457,385 tonnes, Portugal with 83,104 tonnes against 19,080 tonnes and the USA with 24,806 tonnes, up from 2,833 tonnes. In order to fulfill its export obligations, Mauritius has to resort to imports. Imports so far in 1996/97 (June/February) reached 22,746 tonnes, slightly below last year's 27,751 tonnes. The sole country of origin in June/February 1996/97 was South Africa.

ITALY - Sugar imports in December 1996 reached 36,299 tonnes raw value from last year's 21,585 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1996/97 (August/December) up to 170,416 tonnes against 116,043 tonnes in August/December 1995. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 379,026 tonnes, up from 266,279 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in August/December 1996 were Germany with 73,215 tonnes whites against 29,805 tonnes, France with 38,038 tonnes compared to 46,694 tonnes and Brazil with 12,828 tonnes compared to 3,936. Exports in December 1996 reached 11,415 tonnes, up from 9,805 in December 1995

This brought cumulative exports in August/December 1996 up to 65,589 tonnes, down from 139,006 tonnes exported in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 170,210 tonnes against 124,787 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in August/December 1996 were Lebanon with 19,500 tonnes whites against 22,406 tonnes and Croatia with 15,056 tonnes, up from 12,303 tonnes.

India's Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) has invited bids for the allocation of 155,658 tonnes of white sugar out of its annual 1996/97 (October/September) overall government authorized quota of 250,000 tonnes, for which a notice was issued in February. APEDA said it had allocated licenses for the export of 94,342 tonnes of sugar to private traders and the Indian Sugar and General Industry Export Import Corporation (ISGIEC) until April 25, when the new notice was issued. India exported 366,800 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in October/March 1996/97, down from 444,300 tonnes exported the same period in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 (October/September) reached 952,400 tonnes, up from 37,700 the previous year.
